reasoningChain.evidence: Two new rescue routes are available and the newly unlocked warlock creates a visible experiment.
The berserker ranked fourth with only 9.26% damage in the entry fight, while the ranger and mage carried most of the quick clear.
The warlock is described as using damage over time and curses against high-health enemies but has no combat evidence.
The warlock can legally replace the berserker in slot 2 while the ranger, mage, and warrior core remains intact.
This lowers active equipment because the berserker owns three items, but the rescue routes are newly visible opportunities and can reveal whether the warlock's distinct damage style is useful.
If the warlock contributes meaningfully against the rescue enemies, it should supply at least 20% of team damage in the next combat.

hypothesis.problem: The equipped berserker contributed little in the entry fight, and the newly unlocked warlock is untested.
hypothesis.cause: The warlock's damage-over-time and curse pattern may add meaningful damage against tougher rescue enemies.
